755: An SQS search looks for a configuration that minimises the deviation from this target under constraints such as composition, cell size and cell shape. If, for example, a weighted squared error over a chosen cluster set A is used, it can be written as the following optimisation.
756: This is a generic example of an objective function used to explain the purpose. Real tools have their own evaluation functions, such as absolute errors or distances in which the correlations must match exactly. An exact match of the specified correlations or the global optimum is not guaranteed. icet's description of correlations and objective functions
757: At equiatomic composition the mean occupation and the target correlations of all non-empty clusters made of distinct sites are zero. For Al₀.₉Li₀.₁ with Li = +1 the mean occupation is −0.8, the pair correlation 0.64 and the triplet correlation −0.512. These are the theoretical targets of the random alloy, not measured values of a generated structure.
758: With several sublattices, the composition and allowed elements are specified per sublattice and the target is the product of the site averages under independent occupation. In multicomponent systems a binary occupation variable is not enough and several site basis functions are used.

775: Procedure for handing 02A over to the subsequent calculations
776: Decide the parent lattice, the mixing sublattices, and the allowed elements and occupation fractions on each sublattice. Do not build SQS for a perfectly ordered, defect-free line phase.
777: Choose a cell in which the target composition can be represented with an integer number of atoms. For Al₀.₉Li₀.₁, for example, make the total atom count a multiple of 10. Also consider the cell shape and the correlation range.
778: Specify the correlation types and distances to search, the number of trials and the random seed, and generate several candidates.
779: Check the correlation errors, the actual composition, the dependence on atom count and the differences between candidates. Since the objective functions differ between tools, do not compare different tools by their optimisation score alone.
780: Save the unrelaxed SQS, then relax it with the MLIP and pass it to the aiida-alamode phonon/QHA or to the calphy solid-phase TI. If the phase changed during relaxation, do not treat it as data of the original phase.
781: Save the structure, the generation tool and its version, the cell, composition, correlation settings, seed and evaluation results. Whether a configurational term is added to the free energy of the fixed configuration is made consistent in 04A.
782: The MC in an SQS search is an optimisation that minimises the correlation error. Its purpose differs from a physical MC that follows the configurational energy at a real temperature. An SQS alone does not give the configurational entropy, the temperature dependence of short-range order or the solubility range.
783: This section describes tool selection and calculation design. icet 4.0 and sqsgenerator 0.5.6 were installed, and for the Al–Li fcc solid solution icet's fixed-supercell MC (generate_sqs_from_supercells, 32 and 64 atoms) was used in example 6. The difference between a 64-atom SQS and the average of two 32-atom random configurations is −3 to +1 meV/atom for fcc Al–Li at 800 K (ftphase.html 3.6). The sqsgenerator 0.5.6 wrapper (ftphase.structures.sqs_sqsgenerator) had its API fixed and was verified on 2026-10-23 (section 9: at 64 atoms the difference from icet is ≤ 1.2 meV/atom, generation is 20 times faster, and the cluster-vector residual is smaller with icet).

785: 02A and 02B are the stages that prepare the composition and structure series. Learning the interactions and the configurational statistics by MC connect to the subsequent free-energy evaluation. "Assuming a fixed composition as a line phase" and "examining defects and verifying that the composition width is small" are distinguished.
786: Purpose: what is to be obtained
788: Comment: position of the subsequent calculations and MC
789: Obtain the temperature-dependent free energy of a perfectly ordered line phase
790: Expand and relax the ordered structure at fixed composition. On the QHA route, build structures at several volumes.
791: Proceed to the QHA of 03A or to the calphy solid-phase TI. In the perfectly ordered, defect-free approximation no configurational MC is needed. This is distinct from verifying that there is no composition width.
792: First evaluate the disordered solid solution in the ideal-mixing approximation
793: Compute SQS or several random configurations per composition and add the ideal configurational term.
794: 03A handles the free energy of the fixed configuration, 04A the configurational term. Check the atom count, correlations and configuration samples. The SQS itself does not provide the configurational entropy.
795: Examine the defects that carry the off-stoichiometry of an ordered phase
796: Introduce anti-sites and vacancies on each sublattice and evaluate the energy while varying the defect number, distance and arrangement.
797: If the defects are dilute and interact weakly, approximate by the defect energies plus the ideal configurational term of the sublattice. Check the validity at finite concentration.
798: Include configurational correlations, ordering and defect-defect interactions
799: Derive the effective CE interactions from the configurational energies and perform MC with free-energy integration. A validated MLIP-based MC is also an option.
800: Refines the configurational statistics of 04A. The mean energy from MC alone is not an absolute free energy. Do not double-count the vibrational and ideal-mixing contributions.
801: Obtain the liquid-phase free energy from atomistic calculations
802: Melt and equilibrate each composition with the MLIP, then run MD and thermodynamic integration with calphy.
803: Proceed from 02B to 03B. Check diffusion, stationarity and the convergence of the integration. An ordinary lattice CE is not a model that represents diffusion in the liquid.
804: Skip free-energy calculations by using existing data
805: Adopt a CALPHAD model of the target phase and make the reference states consistent.
806: For the liquid this replaces the melting of 02B and the MD/TI of 03B. It can also be used for solid phases. It merges into 05, and the phase equilibrium of 06 is still computed.
807: Determine the final solubility ranges and phase boundaries
808: Align the free energies of all candidate phases and compute the lower convex hull and common tangents.
809: Done in 06. The defect concentration of a single phase, the range over which the structure is retained, or the specified composition range alone do not fix the solubility limit.
810: Concrete order for examining the composition width of an ordered phase
811: For an AB compound, for example, define B substitution on the A sublattice, A substitution on the B sublattice and vacancies on each sublattice as candidates.
812: Build not only single defects but also defect pairs and multi-defect arrangements, relax them with the MLIP and evaluate the energies. Check that they can be mapped back onto the parent lattice after relaxation.
813: Consider whether the independent-defect approximation suffices. If necessary, fit the configurational energies to a CE and validate it on structures outside the training set and on low-energy configurations.
814: Sample configurations with a CE or a suitably defined MLIP-based MC and obtain the free energy by integration etc. with a defined reference state.
815: Make the vibrational contribution consistent and compute the common tangents with the competing solid and liquid phases. Do not fix the solubility limit from the defect concentration of a single phase alone.
816: σ is the occupation configuration, Φ the cluster basis functions and J the effective interactions. In this formula degeneracies etc. are included in the definition of J. Check the per-site or per-cell normalisation of the implementation, and in the presence of vacancies convert to quantities per real atom. A CE is not necessarily built from an MLIP; it is an option for fast evaluation of many configurations on a lattice.

The monte_carlo block is a setting that inserts species swaps into the MD during alchemical/composition integration, with n_swaps: 0 as the default. 833: The phase-diagram API documents free-energy fitting, common tangents and the handling of line compounds and limited-composition-range phases. Specifying a composition range, however, is not predicting the solubility range from a defect model. The ideal configurational correction depends on the calculation mode, and the public source distinguishes composition-integration data from ordinary free-energy data. Do not judge whether double counting occurs from the option name alone. Phase-diagram API, public source
834: Using calphy does not automatically make the configurational statistics consistent. On the other hand, the statement "calphy can only handle fixed configurations" is also insufficient. State the calculation mode, swap operations and free-energy reference adopted.

It reproduces the Li solubility limit in fcc Al but does not adequately reproduce the Al solubility in the ordered AlLi phase. The exclusion of vacancies is discussed as a candidate cause; it is not a demonstration that adding vacancies solved it. [Menon2024] (original Al–Li paper)
